proposition.claim:
A Stein compact subset has a basis of Stein open neighborhoods. \(\mathcal O(K)\) and \(\mathcal M(K)\) are rings of germs on neighborhoods of \(K\); they are not rings of functions merely on the underlying point set. In §1.1 the paper permits general second-countable complex spaces, without an implicit connectedness or pure-dimension assumption. Normality is local and does not force distinct connected components to have the same dimension.

Theorem 5.1, pp. 26–28, compares cohomology only after taking the directed limit over Stein neighborhoods of \(K\). The algebraic scheme is interiorly of finite type and the sheaf is torsion; either interior properness or interior constructibility is required. Corollary 5.2 removes the neighborhood-limit presentation under properness. These alternatives cannot both be dropped: the source’s Remark 3.10 explicitly gives a counterexample.

For the equivariant application, \(G=\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb C/\mathbb R)\) acts antilinearly. Theorem 5.5 uses a comparison of Hochschild–Serre spectral sequences. The absence of fixed points in Theorem 5.6 is essential: it permits the equivariant Artin vanishing input. The statement of that external input was checked in [Retained latex: \cite[Theorem~2.6]{vanishing}]; taking its compact subset empty and using an empty fixed locus yields the vanishing used here. Its entire proof was not independently reproduced.

Proposition 4.2 is on pp. 23–24. Its proof starts with the normalization \(\nu:\widetilde S\to S\), the points \(\widetilde s_i\) above \(s\), and finite surjections \(p_i:T_i\to\widetilde S\) which kill \(\nu^*\alpha\) over disjoint neighborhoods \(\Omega_i\) of \(\widetilde s_i\). The first sentence on p. 24 asserts that the fiber product over \(S\) of the maps \(\nu\circ p_i\) solves the original problem. The same construction is explicit in the released `compactStein.tex`, line 1299 (one-based). The essential inference is \[p_i^*\nu^*\alpha=0\ \hbox{over }p_i^{-1}(\Omega_i\setminus\nu^{-1}Z)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 p^*\alpha=0\ \hbox{near }p^{-1}(s)\setminus p^{-1}Z\] for \(p:\prod_S T_i\to S\). It need not hold.

The algebraic scheme is interiorly of finite type and the sheaf is torsion; either interior properness or interior constructibility is required. Corollary 5.2 removes the neighborhood-limit presentation under properness. These alternatives cannot both be dropped: the source’s Remark 3.10 explicitly gives a counterexample.
